--[[
AchaeaTalismans - see how far your talisman pieces get you.
It reads what the game prints for five TALISMAN commands, keeps it, and draws a window from it:
TALISMAN PIECES what you hold, grouped by talisman TALISMAN PIECES <t> the same for one talisman TALISMAN INFO <t> what a talisman is built from TALISMAN SET <set> which talismans a set holds TALISMAN SETS every set, and how many of each you have done TALISMAN LIST the same sets, plus the talismans you have done
Nothing has to be typed differently: the package reads those whenever they are typed, by you or by `tals scan`. Reading is all it does unless asked to scan, and a scan sends only TALISMAN commands, plus MORE while one of them is paged.
The arithmetic is HELP TALISMANS (19.24): "Two Pieces of the same level may be combined into a Piece of one level higher", and split back down. So a piece at level n is worth 2^(n-1) level-1 pieces, and a slot that asks for level 7 wants 64 of those. Every piece you hold of a slot's keyword counts toward it, whatever its level, because a higher one can be split down and lower ones combined up. A slot is ready when the sum reaches what it asks for; the COMBINE and SPLIT commands that get it there are still yours to type.
tals show the window, and what has been read so far tals show|hide the window tals all the window lists every talisman you hold pieces of tals set <set> the window lists one set's talismans tals scan TALISMAN SETS and PIECES, then INFO for each talisman you hold pieces of and have not read yet tals scan <set> TALISMAN SET <set>, then INFO for each of its talismans tals stop stop a scan tals diag build stamp, what is stored, where
]]
AchaeaTalismans = AchaeaTalismans or {} local M = AchaeaTalismans
M.VERSION = "0.1.0" M.BUILD = M.BUILD or "source" -- build.py replaces this
-- The name Mudlet knows the package by, which is what its uninstall event -- carries. build.py has the same string; the harness holds the two together. M.PACKAGE = "AchaeaTalismans" M.WINDOW = "AchaeaTalismans"
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------- the data
-- Everything saved, and the type each key must have to come back from a -- file. A key not listed here is neither saved nor loaded, so the two cannot -- disagree. local DATA_KEYS = { sets = "table", -- keyword -> { name, done, total, talismans } setOrder = "table", -- set keywords, in the game's order talismans = "table", -- keyword -> { name, brief, set, pieces } held = "table", -- the last TALISMAN PIECES, one row per line heldAt = "number", -- when that was read, os.time(); 0 for never completed = "table", -- talisman keyword -> { name, set } focus = "string", -- the set the window shows, or "" for all held shown = "boolean", -- whether the window is open }
local function fresh() return { sets = {}, setOrder = {}, talismans = {}, held = {}, heldAt = 0, completed = {}, focus = "", shown = true, } end
M.data = M.data or fresh()
-- On the module table rather than in a file-local: Mudlet keeps temp triggers -- and timers across a script recompile, and a fresh local would lose the ids -- of the old ones and install a second set. M.state = M.state or { triggers = {}, handlers = {}, cap = nil, -- the output being read, if any scan = nil, -- the scan in progress, if any loaded = "none", read = 0, -- outputs read since the package started } local S = M.state
local function log(message, colour) -- A leading newline, because this is often called from a trigger, and -- echo inside a trigger is glued onto the end of the line that fired it. cecho("\n<" .. (colour or "gold") .. ">[talismans]<reset> " .. message .. "\n") end
function M.now() if type(getEpoch) == "function" then local ok, t = pcall(getEpoch) if ok and type(t) == "number" then return t end end return os.time() end
-- ---------------------------------------------------------- saving, loading
function M.path() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/achaea-talismans.lua" end
function M.load() local path = M.path() if not (io.exists and io.exists(path)) then S.loaded = "none" return false end local stored = {} if not pcall(table.load, path, stored) then -- table.load runs the file as Lua, so a half-written one raises. Say so, -- and let M.save move it aside rather than write over it. S.loaded = "unreadable" log("could not read " .. path .. "; starting empty", "red") return false end local data = fresh() for key, kind in pairs(DATA_KEYS) do if type(stored[key]) == kind then data[key] = stored[key] end end M.data = data S.loaded = "ok" return true end
function M.save() local path = M.path() if S.loaded == "unreadable" then -- os.rename reports failure by returning nil, not by raising. If the file -- could not be moved aside, writing now would destroy the only copy. local ok, moved = pcall(os.rename, path, path .. ".bad") if not (ok and moved) then log("could not move " .. path .. " aside; nothing saved", "red") return false end S.loaded = "ok" end local out = {} for key in pairs(DATA_KEYS) do out[key] = M.data[key] end -- table.save reports a file it could not open by returning nil and a -- message, not by raising. So the message is the sign of a failure, and -- pcall's own result is not one. local ok, _, failed = pcall(table.save, path, out) if not ok or failed ~= nil then log("could not write " .. path .. "; what was read lasts until Mudlet closes", "red") return false end return true end
-- ------------------------------------------------------- reading the output
-- Every pattern below is written against a capture of the game's own output, -- typed on 2026-11-16 except where it says otherwise, and applied to a line -- with its trailing spaces removed: the game pads its header lines.
M.HEADERS = { -- TALISMAN PIECES. No indent before Num. pieces = "^Num%s+Name%s+Level%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- TALISMAN PIECES <talisman>. The same columns, indented. tpieces = "^%s+Num%s+Name%s+Level%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- The talisman tables in TALISMAN LIST. tlist = "^Name%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- TALISMAN SETS, and the sets table in TALISMAN LIST. sets = "^Name%s+Status%s+Keyword$", } -- TALISMAN SET and TALISMAN INFO both open with this; the line after it says -- which one it is. M.NAME_LINE = "^Name: (.+)$" -- The tables open and close with a rule of dashes, 79 or 82 long. Twenty is -- enough to tell it from the underlines of a help scroll's headings. M.RULE = "^%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-+$" -- The pager. Everything from the first line to the second is the client -- paging, and whatever arrived meanwhile is not part of the table. M.MORE_OPEN = "^%[Type MORE if you wish to continue reading" M.MORE_CLOSE = "^%[File continued via MORE%]" -- A paged table nobody went on reading is let go after this long, so that a -- later MORE for something else does not feed that something to it. M.PAUSE_MAX = 120
-- B 1 a Black Dragon's heart 1 Dragon blackdragonheart -- The name column is cut at 33 characters, so the name is taken as whatever -- comes before the last three columns rather than by width. M.ROW_PIECES = "^(%u) (%d+)%s+(.-)%s+(%d+)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- blackdragonpieces M.ROW_GROUP = "^%s%s%s%s%s%s(%S+)$" -- B (1) a Silver Dragon's claw 2 dragon silverdragonclaw M.ROW_TPIECES = "^%s+(%u) %((%d+)%) (.-)%s+(%d+)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- a Votive of Rememberance Historica votive M.ROW_TLIST = "^(.-)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- Dragon 0/6 dragon M.ROW_SETS = "^(.-)%s+(%d+)/(%d+)%s+(%S+)$" -- a Black Dragon Talisman (blackdragon) M.ROW_SET = "^(.-) %((%S+)%)$" -- (1) a Red Dragon's claw (reddragonclaw), level 7 -- A long one wraps, with the rest on the next line indented two spaces -- (INFO harness, 2026-10-15), so rows are joined before this is applied. M.ROW_INFO = "^%((%d+)%) (.-) %((%S+)%), level (%d+)$"
local function rtrim(s) return (s:gsub("%s+$", "")) end local function trim(s) return (s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
local function headerKind(l) for kind, pattern in pairs(M.HEADERS) do if l:find(pattern) then return kind end end if l:find(M.NAME_LINE) then return "name" end return nil end
-- Each reader takes a capture and a line and answers with one of: -- nil the line was taken, keep reading -- "done" the line was taken and the output is over -- "pass" the output ended before this line, which is someone else's -- "drop" this was not the output it looked like local READ = {}
local function tableReader(onRow) return function(cap, l) if l:find(M.RULE) then cap.rules = cap.rules + 1 if cap.rules == 2 then return "done" end return nil end -- Before the opening rule nothing else is expected. if cap.rules == 0 then return "drop" end onRow(cap, l) return nil end end
READ.pieces = tableReader(function(cap, l) local src, n, name, level, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_PIECES) if src then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { source = src, count = tonumber(n), name = trim(name), level = tonumber(level), set = set, kw = kw, group = cap.group, } return end local heading = l:match(M.ROW_GROUP) if heading then -- The heading is the talisman's keyword with "pieces" on the end, as far -- as the six dragons show; the others are read the same way. cap.group = heading:gsub("pieces$", "") end end)
READ.tpieces = tableReader(function(cap, l) local src, n, name, level, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_TPIECES) if src then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { source = src, count = tonumber(n), name = trim(name), level = tonumber(level), set = set, kw = kw, } end end)
READ.tlist = tableReader(function(cap, l) local name, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_TLIST) if name and name ~= "" then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = trim(name), set = set, kw = kw } end end)
READ.sets = tableReader(function(cap, l) local name, done, total, kw = l:match(M.ROW_SETS) if name then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = trim(name), done = tonumber(done), total = tonumber(total), kw = kw, } end end)
-- The line after "Name:" decides between a set and a talisman. READ.name = function(cap, l) local partial = l:match("^Partial name: (%S+)$") if partial then cap.kind, cap.kw, cap.rows = "set", partial, {} return nil end local kw = l:match("^Keyword: (%S+)$") if kw then cap.kind, cap.kw, cap.pieces = "info", kw, {} return nil end return "drop" end
READ.set = function(cap, l) if cap.listing then local name, kw = l:match(M.ROW_SET) if name then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = name, kw = kw } return nil end return "pass" end if l == "Talismans:" then cap.listing = true; return nil end local desc = l:match("^Description: (.*)$") if desc then cap.description = desc; return nil end if l:find("^ ") and cap.description then cap.description = cap.description .. " " .. trim(l) return nil end return "pass" end
local function flushPiece(cap) if not cap.pending then return end local n, name, kw, level = cap.pending:match(M.ROW_INFO) if n then cap.pieces[#cap.pieces + 1] = { count = tonumber(n), name = name, kw = kw, level = tonumber(level), } else cap.unread = (cap.unread or 0) + 1 end cap.pending = nil end
READ.info = function(cap, l) local set = l:match("^Set: (.*)$") if set then flushPiece(cap) cap.set = trim(set) return "done" end if l == "Pieces:" then cap.listing = true; return nil end local brief = l:match("^Brief: (.*)$") if brief then cap.brief = brief; return nil end if l:find("^ ") then if cap.pending then cap.pending = cap.pending .. " " .. trim(l) elseif cap.brief and not cap.listing then cap.brief = cap.brief .. " " .. trim(l) end return nil end if cap.listing and l:find("^%(%d+%) ") then flushPiece(cap) cap.pending = l return nil end flushPiece(cap) return "pass" end
-- -------------------------------------------------- folding what was read in
--- The set keyword for a set as some listing names it: TALISMAN PIECES says --- "Dragon", TALISMAN PIECES <t> says "dragon", TALISMAN INFO says "Dragon", --- and Miscellaneous's keyword is "misc". function M.setKey(name) if not name then return nil end local low = name:lower() if M.data.sets[low] then return low end for kw, set in pairs(M.data.sets) do if (set.name or ""):lower() == low then return kw end end return low end
--- Which talisman a piece keyword belongs to: TALISMAN INFO says for certain, --- and failing that the heading it was last listed under. function M.ownerOf(pieceKw) for tkw, t in pairs(M.data.talismans) do for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do if p.kw == pieceKw then return tkw end end end for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.kw == pieceKw and row.group then return row.group end end return nil end
local COMMIT = {}
COMMIT.pieces = function(cap) M.data.held = cap.rows M.data.heldAt = os.time() end
-- One talisman's pieces replace what was held for that talisman, and only -- that. Which talisman is worked out from the rows, since the output does -- not name it. COMMIT.tpieces = function(cap) local owner, mixed = nil, false for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do local o = M.ownerOf(row.kw) if o == nil or (owner and o ~= owner) then mixed = true end owner = owner or o row.group = o end local gone = {} if owner and not mixed then for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.group == owner then gone[row] = true end end else local kws = {} for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do kws[row.kw] = true end for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if kws[row.kw] then gone[row] = true end end end local held, placed = {}, false for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if gone[row] then if not placed then for _, new in ipairs(cap.rows) do held[#held + 1] = new end placed = true end else held[#held + 1] = row end end if not placed then for _, new in ipairs(cap.rows) do held[#held + 1] = new end end M.data.held = held end
-- Talismans in these tables are done: HELP TALISMANS says TALISMAN LIST -- shows the completed ones and the completed ones you carry. Added to, never -- cleared, because which table is which is not printed. COMMIT.tlist = function(cap) for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do M.data.completed[row.kw] = { name = row.name, set = row.set } end end
COMMIT.sets = function(cap) local order = {} for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do local set = M.data.sets[row.kw] or {} set.name, set.done, set.total = row.name, row.done, row.total M.data.sets[row.kw] = set order[#order + 1] = row.kw end M.data.setOrder = order end
COMMIT.set = function(cap) local key = M.data.sets[cap.kw] and cap.kw or M.setKey(cap.name) local set = M.data.sets[key] or {} set.name = cap.name set.talismans = cap.rows set.description = cap.description M.data.sets[key] = set for _, kw in ipairs(M.data.setOrder) do if kw == key then return end end M.data.setOrder[#M.data.setOrder + 1] = key end
COMMIT.info = function(cap) M.data.talismans[cap.kw] = { name = cap.name, brief = cap.brief, set = cap.set, pieces = cap.pieces, } end
function M.commit(cap) if not COMMIT[cap.kind] then return false end COMMIT[cap.kind](cap) S.read = S.read + 1 M.save() M.scanHeard(cap) M.redraw() return true end
local function open(l) local kind = headerKind(l) if not kind then return end if kind == "name" then S.cap = { kind = "name", name = l:match(M.NAME_LINE) } else S.cap = { kind = kind, rules = 0, rows = {} } end end
--- One line of game output. Everything the package knows comes through here. function M.feed(text) local l = rtrim(text or "") local cap = S.cap if l:find(M.MORE_OPEN) then if cap then cap.paused, cap.pausedAt = true, M.now() if S.scan then send("more", false) end end return end if l:find(M.MORE_CLOSE) then if cap then if cap.paused and M.now() - (cap.pausedAt or 0) > M.PAUSE_MAX then S.cap = nil else cap.paused = false end end return end -- A new listing starting means a table or a paged output was never -- finished, and it is let go. An unpaged SET or INFO is left to its reader, -- which ends it on any line it does not know. if cap and (cap.rules or cap.paused) and headerKind(l) then S.cap, cap = nil, nil end if cap and cap.paused then return end if cap then local verdict = READ[cap.kind](cap, l) if verdict == nil then return end S.cap = nil if verdict == "done" then M.commit(cap); return end if verdict == "pass" then M.commit(cap) end -- "pass" and "drop" both leave this line to be looked at afresh. end open(l) end
-- ------------------------------------------------------------- the arithmetic
--- A piece at this level, in level-1 pieces. function M.units(level) return 2 ^ ((tonumber(level) or 1) - 1) end
--- Every held piece of this keyword, in level-1 pieces. function M.heldUnits(pieceKw) local n = 0 for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.kw == pieceKw then n = n + row.count * M.units(row.level) end end return n end
local function label(tkw, pieceKw) if pieceKw:sub(1, #tkw) == tkw and #pieceKw > #tkw then return pieceKw:sub(#tkw + 1) end return pieceKw end
--- How far the pieces held get one talisman, from its TALISMAN INFO. function M.progress(tkw) local t = M.data.talismans[tkw] if not t then return nil end local slots, ready, have, need = {}, 0, 0, 0 for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do local want = p.count * M.units(p.level) local got = M.heldUnits(p.kw) local counted = math.min(got, want) slots[#slots + 1] = { kw = p.kw, label = label(tkw, p.kw), level = p.level, count = p.count, have = got, need = want, } if got >= want then ready = ready + 1 end have, need = have + counted, need + want end return { slots = slots, ready = ready, have = have, need = need } end
--- "done", "started" or "none". function M.status(tkw) if M.data.completed[tkw] then return "done" end local t = M.data.talismans[tkw] for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.group == tkw then return "started" end if t then for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do if p.kw == row.kw then return "started" end end end end return "none" end
--- Talisman keywords you hold pieces of, in the order TALISMAN PIECES listed --- them. function M.heldTalismans() local out, seen = {}, {} for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do local tkw = row.group or M.ownerOf(row.kw) if tkw and not seen[tkw] then seen[tkw] = true out[#out + 1] = tkw end end return out end
-- -------------------------------------------------------------- the drawing
M.BAR = 16 local MARK = { done = "<green>●", started = "<yellow>◐", none = "<dim_grey>○" }
local function bar(have, need) local fill = need > 0 and math.floor(M.BAR * math.min(have, need) / need) or 0 if have > 0 and fill == 0 then fill = 1 end local colour = have >= need and "<green>" or (have > 0 and "<yellow>" or "<dim_grey>") return colour .. string.rep("█", fill) .. "<dim_grey>" .. string.rep("░", M.BAR - fill) end
local function pad(s, n) if #s >= n then return s:sub(1, n) end return s .. string.rep(" ", n - #s) end
local function fmt(n) return string.format("%d", n) end
--- What the window shows, as a list of pieces: a string is coloured text, --- a table is { text, code, hint } and becomes a link that runs the code. function M.render() local out = {} local function add(s) out[#out + 1] = s end local function link(text, code, hint) out[#out + 1] = { text, code, hint } end local d = M.data
add("<white>Talisman pieces<reset>") if d.heldAt > 0 then add("<dim_grey> read " .. os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", d.heldAt) .. " ") else add("<dim_grey> pieces not read yet ") end link("<cyan>[scan]", "AchaeaTalismans.scan()", "send TALISMAN SETS, PIECES, and INFO for what you hold") add(" ") link("<cyan>[all]", "AchaeaTalismans.setFocus('')", "every talisman you hold pieces of") add("\n\n")
local list if d.focus ~= "" then local set = d.sets[d.focus] local name = set and set.name or d.focus add("<white>" .. name .. "<reset>") if set and set.total then add(" " .. fmt(set.done) .. "/" .. fmt(set.total) .. " done") end add(" ") link("<cyan>[scan set]", "AchaeaTalismans.scan('" .. d.focus .. "')", "send TALISMAN SET and INFO for each of its talismans") add("\n") list = {} if set and set.talismans then for _, t in ipairs(set.talismans) do list[#list + 1] = t.kw end else for tkw, t in pairs(d.talismans) do if M.setKey(t.set) == d.focus then list[#list + 1] = tkw end end table.sort(list) if #list == 0 then add("<dim_grey> its talismans are not read yet\n") end end else list = M.heldTalismans() if #list == 0 then add("<dim_grey>No pieces read yet. TALISMAN PIECES, or [scan].\n") end end
for _, tkw in ipairs(list) do local t = d.talismans[tkw] local status = M.status(tkw) add("\n" .. MARK[status] .. " <white>" .. (t and t.name or tkw) .. "<reset> <dim_grey>(" .. tkw .. ")") local p = M.progress(tkw) if status == "done" then add(" <green>done\n") elseif p then local pct = p.need > 0 and math.floor(100 * p.have / p.need) or 0 add(" <reset>" .. fmt(p.ready) .. "/" .. fmt(#p.slots) .. " ready, " .. fmt(pct) .. "%\n") for _, s in ipairs(p.slots) do local count = s.count > 1 and (fmt(s.count) .. "x") or "" add(" <reset>" .. pad(s.label, 16) .. " <dim_grey>" .. pad(count .. "L" .. fmt(s.level), 5) .. " ") add(bar(s.have, s.need) .. " <reset>" .. fmt(s.have) .. "/" .. fmt(s.need) .. "\n") end else add(" <dim_grey>needs not read ") link("<cyan>[info]", "send('talisman info " .. tkw .. "', false)", "TALISMAN INFO " .. tkw) add("\n") for _, row in ipairs(d.held) do if row.group == tkw then add(" <reset>" .. pad(label(tkw, row.kw), 16) .. " <dim_grey>" .. fmt(row.count) .. " at L" .. fmt(row.level) .. " = " .. fmt(row.count * M.units(row.level)) .. "\n") end end end end
if #d.setOrder > 0 then add("\n<white>Sets<reset> <dim_grey>click one to list its talismans\n") for _, kw in ipairs(d.setOrder) do local set = d.sets[kw] link("<reset>" .. pad(set.name or kw, 14), "AchaeaTalismans.setFocus('" .. kw .. "')", "list the " .. (set.name or kw) .. " set") local line = " <dim_grey>" .. pad(fmt(set.done or 0) .. "/" .. fmt(set.total or 0), 6) if set.talismans then for _, t in ipairs(set.talismans) do line = line .. MARK[M.status(t.kw)] end end add(line .. "\n") end else add("\n<dim_grey>Sets not read yet. TALISMAN SETS, or [scan].\n") end return out end
--- Draw the pieces M.render made into a window, or the main console for nil. function M.draw(win) for _, piece in ipairs(M.render()) do if type(piece) == "table" then if win then cechoLink(win, piece[1], piece[2], piece[3], true) else cechoLink(piece[1], piece[2], piece[3], true) end else if win then cecho(win, piece) else cecho(piece) end end end end
function M.redraw() if not M.data.shown then return false end openUserWindow(M.WINDOW, true, true, "right") pcall(setUserWindowTitle, M.WINDOW, "Talismans") clearWindow(M.WINDOW) M.draw(M.WINDOW) return true end
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------- scanning
-- A scan sends one command, waits for its output to be read, and only then -- sends the next, so two outputs never arrive tangled and the game is never -- flooded. One that has not answered in this long is given up on. M.SCAN_WAIT = 8
local function scanSend() local scan = S.scan local step = table.remove(scan.queue, 1) if not step then S.scan = nil log("scan done: " .. scan.heard .. " read" .. (scan.missed > 0 and (", " .. scan.missed .. " not answered") or "")) return end scan.step = step send(step.cmd, false) scan.timer = tempTimer(M.SCAN_WAIT, function() M.scanTimeout() end) end
local function infoFor(list) local steps = {} for _, tkw in ipairs(list) do steps[#steps + 1] = { cmd = "talisman info " .. tkw, kind = "info", kw = tkw } end return steps end
function M.scan(setKw) M.stopScan(true) local queue if setKw and setKw ~= "" then setKw = setKw:lower() queue = { { cmd = "talisman set " .. setKw, kind = "set", then_ = "setInfo" } } M.data.focus = M.data.sets[setKw] and setKw or M.data.focus else queue = { { cmd = "talisman sets", kind = "sets" }, { cmd = "talisman pieces", kind = "pieces", then_ = "heldInfo" }, } end S.scan = { queue = queue, heard = 0, missed = 0 } scanSend() return true end
--- A capture was read; if the scan was waiting for one like it, move on. function M.scanHeard(cap) local scan = S.scan if not (scan and scan.step and scan.step.kind == cap.kind) then return false end -- INFO for some other talisman, typed meanwhile, is not the answer. if scan.step.kw and cap.kw ~= scan.step.kw then return false end if scan.timer then pcall(killTimer, scan.timer); scan.timer = nil end scan.heard = scan.heard + 1 local after = scan.step.then_ if after == "heldInfo" then local todo = {} for _, tkw in ipairs(M.heldTalismans()) do if not M.data.talismans[tkw] then todo[#todo + 1] = tkw end end for _, step in ipairs(infoFor(todo)) do scan.queue[#scan.queue + 1] = step end elseif after == "setInfo" then local list = {} for _, t in ipairs(cap.rows or {}) do list[#list + 1] = t.kw end for _, step in ipairs(infoFor(list)) do scan.queue[#scan.queue + 1] = step end local key = M.data.sets[cap.kw] and cap.kw or M.setKey(cap.name) M.data.focus = key end scan.step = nil scanSend() return true end
function M.scanTimeout() local scan = S.scan if not scan then return end scan.timer = nil scan.missed = scan.missed + 1 scan.step = nil scanSend() end
